text: You download a new app, eager to use its features. You just want to get started quickly, without hassle. A buzz of anticipation as you tap the icon.
Immediately, a screen appears. A long list of permissions: location, camera, microphone, contacts. All of them, right there, all at once.
You pause. Why does a simple app need *everything*? You might suspect it's just greedy, or overreaching for your data.
But the system learned: users abandon apps when interrupted too much. Each individual request creates friction, causing people to quit.
So, platforms bundled these requests. One big 'Accept' instead of many small ones. The cost? You often grant more access than you truly intend.
Tomorrow, you'll still tap 'Accept.' But now, you see the hidden bargain. You understand this invisible system of bundled choices.
